defect_observations.observation: Route verified (main.tex 40 and 64; parts/p15.tex 45; annex/p15.tex 44). The two driver files now hash 2c6f3003... and f05d881f..., not the 9B7AC188... and A395BEA5... recorded in packet w02b-p15-021; the section files themselves match the queue hashes.

Packet w02b-p15-021 records reader_evidence for 163.6 only at annex lines 1-463 and 512-554; the proofs owed for C016-C019 (annex 555-800) lie outside that recorded read extent. This audit read them in full.

C001 is stated for positive integer n, while the Poisson and gamma parts of C002 apply 'the lemma' for positive real n tending to infinity without saying that real-indexed families reduce to integer-indexed sequences; the index-free estimate at annex 10-14 supports the step.

The source's Lemma 1 states uniformity on every closed interval (book p. 219). The body restates this as compact intervals and adds the uniformly continuous variant, with the whole-line counterexample at C019 item 2. It does not say outright that this qualifies the source's wording.

The binomial reciprocity identity (source (1.10)) is never displayed in body or annex, yet the C006 (annex 97) and C008 (annex 192-196) proofs invoke it by name. It is derivable from the displayed differences of theta^r.
The source's printed (3.3) has exponent r-k (book p. 224, visually checked). The handbook states exponent r and notes only 'no subtraction of k'; the printed variant itself is not named.
The C012 annex proof establishes existence and uniqueness but does not cite the necessity half of 'exactly when'. That half is proved in the C010 annex at 231-238.

C016 obtains exchangeability through 'the same numerator-permutation argument as in the direct urn proof' rather than by citing the exchangeability conclusion of thm:p15-polya-word-law (polya-urns-and-beta-prediction.tex 71-72) for this identical urn. It asserts the agreement with that theorem ('agree algebraically') without writing the general-k gamma-ratio line. Positivity of r depends on reading 'positive black weight b, red weight r' (body 345) as applying to both weights.

In C017, uniqueness of lambda is transferred in one sentence. The step showing that a competing lambda' induces a competing directing law with the same finite-coordinate probabilities is not written. Convergence of singleton frequencies relies on the determining class without saying that singletons are obtainable from it. The empirical-frequency clause also goes beyond the source's Generalizations paragraph (book p. 229), although the entry is titled as the stated generalization.
The C018 occupancy argument treats only binary (Bernoulli) mixing laws. The one-line reduction of a general identical-independent mixture to almost-surely binary components is not written.
The C014 harmonic comparison leaves boundedness of C^(1/(2n)) unstated. It holds because C >= m_0 = 1.
